result:
Reviewed the 4-commit range `main...HEAD` (6 files: CSP dev `unsafe-eval`, tension `between` streaming guard, a new panel test, and two comment-only edits). The working tree is clean, so nothing extra in scope. Note: `node_modules` is not installed in this environment, so I could not execute the test suite or `tsc`; findings are from static analysis.

The two functional changes are correct in substance — `t.between &&` does prevent the `TypeError` on partial-streamed tensions, and gating `'unsafe-eval'` behind `NODE_ENV !== "production"` keeps the production CSP eval-free. Two issues worth flagging (the ReportFindings tool was not available in my toolset, so findings are inline below):

**Findings**

- `/repo/proxy.test.ts:12` — medium. The security tripwire no longer covers the production code path. `proxy()` (`/repo/proxy.ts:53`) calls `buildCsp(nonce)` with one argument, so the shipped CSP is decided entirely by the default parameter `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`/repo/proxy.ts:28`). Every assertion in this file now pins the flag explicitly (`buildCsp(NONCE, false)` / `buildCsp(NONCE, true)`), so nothing tests the default. Concrete scenario: someone typos the default to `process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"` (or flips it to `true` while debugging a dev build); all four tests still pass and the production build silently ships `script-src ... 'unsafe-eval'`, defeating the `'strict-dynamic'` nonce policy the file's header comment says must "fail loudly in tests rather than silently shipping". Same exposure if a build is run with `NODE_ENV=development` explicitly set in the environment (Next only defaults `NODE_ENV` when unset, it does not force it). Fix: add a case that stubs the env (`vi.stubEnv("NODE_ENV", "production")`) and asserts `buildCsp(NONCE)` — the zero-arg form — contains no `'unsafe-eval'`.

- `/repo/app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.tsx:113` — low. The guard is truthiness-based, but the partial-JSON parser used for streaming previews (`parsePartialJson` in `/repo/app/hooks/useArtifactGeneration.ts:75`) closes open arrays, so mid-stream `between` legitimately takes the values `[]` and `["A"]`, not just `undefined`. `[]` is truthy, so for the frames where only `"between": [` has arrived the panel renders a bare `↔` row with two empty spans, and for `["A"]` it renders `A ↔` with a dangling arrow — the same half-baked endpoint display the fix set out to avoid (no crash, purely visual). `t.between?.length === 2` (or `t.between?.[0] && t.between?.[1]`) covers all three partial states. The new test at `/repo/app/components/panels/BalancedPerspectivesPanel.test.tsx:46` only exercises the fully-absent case, so these two intermediate states are untested.
